chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The one who mentions Me in a gathering of the people, I shall mention him in a gathering of the Angels.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for mentioning Allah in a gathering of people?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (as) underscores the spiritual merit of public dhikr, linking human remembrance in earthly assemblies to divine acknowledgment in the celestial realm. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the continuity between the visible world and the unseen, where social acts of worship are mirrored by angelic presence, reinforcing the concept of divine reciprocity (muqabalah) in devotional practices.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “The one who mentions Me<sup>azwj</sup> in a gathering of the people, I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Mention him in a gathering of the Angels’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, “Whoever speaks of Me in a group of people, I speak of him in a group of angels.’”
